title: Revocation fetch loop has no cap on URLs tried: unbounded validation latency
description:
extract_cdp_http_urls and extract_aia_http_urls return every HTTP/HTTPS URL a certificate advertises, with no limit, and all four fetchers plus both cache wrappers try every one sequentially until one yields a determinative verdict.

Memory is not the concern; latency is. Each attempt carries the transport's own timeout, so total time for one check is (number of URLs) x (timeout). A certificate listing 500 dead CDP URLs against a 10s timeout hangs a single path validation for well over an hour, inside pkix_chain::verify_chain, with no way for the caller to bound it. The accumulated per-URL failure string grows with it and is propagated in RevocationFetchFailed.description.

Exposure is gated behind 'a CA issued this certificate': revocation checking runs after path signature validation, so the extensions are whatever some trusted issuer signed. Public CAs will not issue a cert with hundreds of CDP URLs; a private or unsanitised CA might, and the field is the kind of thing nobody validates. Sibling issue PKIX-rm8.43 files the same class for the AIA certificate-fetch loop (no aggregate byte cap), so the pattern is already recognised in the workspace.

Candidate fix: a documented cap on attempts per check (the loop already stops at the first success, so a cap only bites when URLs are failing), and/or an overall deadline for one revocation check rather than a per-request timeout. The cap value is a policy choice and should be stated, not implicit.

Found while working PKIX-cr8; not one of the ten issues that epic was filed with.
